result.title: Can Open Source Make AI Agents Safer?
result.description:
Hugging Face co-founder Thomas Wolf and ServiceNow’s Amanda Grady, SVP of AI Platform Security, join the NVIDIA AI Podcast to explain how to keep AI agents safe when telling a model “please don’t” is no longer enough.

They cover why firm boundaries beat persuadable models, what happened when Hugging Face was attacked by a swarm of AI agents, and why security is what lets companies put agents to real work. This is the 15-minute best-moments edit. The full-length episode is on your favorite podcast platform! 

In this episode:
0:16 Why guardrails inside the model aren’t enough
2:00 The attack on Hugging Face, and why open models mattered
3:28 Agent identity and the AI Passport
6:03 Security as an unlocker for AI
8:33 Why open source is more secure, not less
10:59 Physical AI and the micro-duck
13:12 Fine-tuning for everyone
14:11 Who gets to build AI

Guests
Thomas Wolf, Co-founder, Hugging Face
Amanda Grady, SVP, AI Platform Security, ServiceNow

result.title: NVIDIA cuPhoton Brings Real-Time Black Hole Science to GPUs
result.description:
NVIDIA cuPhoton moves the scientific data pipeline onto GPUs, helping researchers study black holes as events unfold.

- Eight radio observatories worked together as a virtual telescope the size of Earth to capture the first image of a black hole in the M87 galaxy
- cuPhoton streams only the data needed for black hole jets and overlaps loading with signal processing, reconstruction, analysis and visualization, all of which AI agents can run
- It speeds up data loading by up to 3,700x and correlation by up to 460x, scaling across multi-node systems powered by the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform
- Data can now be acquired at rates up to 345 GHz, cuPhoton reduces months of compute to minutes and  help  resolve the light rings around black hole

Learn More: https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/high-performance-computing/ai-for-science/cuphoton/
